messages:
Elena: Quick thread  we need a battlecard refresh focused on three buyer archetypes: platform eng, product PMs, and infra SREs. Can we split bullets accordingly?

Ravi: Agree. I'll draft top-line claims per archetype. For platform engs: 'single API for model routing, local private deploys, and deterministic latency SLOs.'

Sam: For PMs keep it outcome oriented: 'Ship features faster — smaller infra teams, fewer vendor contracts.' Short and benefit-led.

Claire: SREs will push back on scale and reliability. Add a small section on failover: canary -> quantized local -> hosted fallback. Include a quick diagram in the one-pager.

Elena: Good call. Also want a 3-line "what to say" opener for SDRs and AEs. Ravi, can you give 2 variants — one technical, one business?

Ravi: Technical opener: "We provide a unified inference plane with predictable P95 at scale and routing policies for cost/latency tradeoffs."

Ravi: Business opener: "We reduce engineering toil and inference spend so your product team ships features faster."

Sam: Add objection handlers (30s scripts). Example: Customer: 'We use cloud native endpoints' -> Reply: 'Cloud endpoints are great for burst. Redwood gives workload predictability and the operational contracts you need for SLAs.'

Claire: Another: 'We're worried about lock-in' -> Reply: 'Our routing and model portability let you move traffic between hosted, dedicated, and private without rewriting your app.'

Elena: For the webinar benchmark narrative we must be careful with vendor mentions. Draft structure: 1) customer problem 2) methodology briefly (qps, seq len, model family) 3) demo results as relative multipliers 4) live rollback demo 5) appendix with raw configs.

Ravi: Methodology blurb: "Test harness: steady qps streams (5, 20, 100 qps), seq len 64/256, model family: open 13B vs Redwood-quantized variant. Results reported as median and p95; cost normalized per 1k tokens."

Sam: Legal note: use "up to" language and include test caveats. We'll avoid direct named-competitor callouts.

Claire: For the demo script I'll write a deterministic failure: inject an artificial latency spike into the canary pool, show automatic policy triggers, and route to the next tier. We'll show the routing log and the console.

Elena: Nice. For SDR routing, here's a compact scoring snippet we can use in the ops workflow (Ravi please convert to prod-ready later):
```
scoring:
  latency_complaint: 60
  sla_mandate: 25
  on_prem_requirement: 15
queues:
  inbound_sdr: "score<50"
  sd_ops_triage: "score>=50 and score<80"
  enterprise_ae: "score>=80"
```

Ravi: I'll pair that with an email template for handoff. Also propose tagging leads with "priority-demo" when score>70 so AMs can fast-track book time.

Sam: A/B test ideas for the launch email: Subject A: "Cut inference unpredictability" Subject B: "Make model latency predictable" Open->demo conversion is the KPI.

Claire: Battlecard one-pager should have 5-second claim, 30-second elevator, top 6 rebuttals, routing rules snippet, and one screenshot of console alerts. Keep it printable.

Elena: Deadlines: Ravi final copy by 2pm PT, Sam slides and demo script by 5pm PT, Claire failover runbook by EOD. Ops-bot will confirm hosting for demo environment.

ops-bot: Demo env provisioned at https://staging.redwood.ai/demo (expires in 48h) :gear:

Ravi: Quick question : do we want an explicit "cost savings" claim or just relative performance?

Elena: Use relative multipliers only e.g. "up to 2.5x lower per-token latency under typical app loads" and include methodology. No absolute $ numbers in public collateral.

Sam: I'll add a slide showing sample query mix to make the test believable (chat-like vs batch embeddings).

Claire: I'll prep the console screenshots and annotated logs for the appendix.

Elena: Thanks. Small follow-up: can we add one customer quote placeholder for the deck (can be anonymized) that speaks to 'reduced rollout risk' and 'predictable performance'? I'll coordinate with cs.

Ravi: On it. Will ping CS for a short anonymized blurb.

Elena: Great. Reconvene 3pm PT for review. :white_check_mark:
